title: tests.py's pytest worker count is chosen from timings at -n 4, 6 and 8 under the host lock
goal: A recorded run of the full tests.py at -n 4, 6 and 8 on the same host, each under the host lock, shows which worker count is fastest on a 4-core and an 8-core host, and tests.py's default follows it (physical cores, logical cores or a cap), with a test named worker_count_default that plants a core count and sees the chosen n. Found by ST-5q5b5qtz, which landed ordering only: its worker-count data was one -n 8 run of 1106 s on the Windows 4-core host.
